answer: The most convincing sybil defense binds each agent identity to a nonce-chained work history: every completed task appends a signed hash of the previous record plus a fresh nonce, so an attacker cannot fork one reputation into parallel copies without recomputing the entire chain. Like a quartz vein running through rock, the history is linear and immutable; a meadow of duplicate agents all share one chain, while the terrace of costly verifiable work each block requires makes forgery economically pointless.
